newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains hit by sterling strength.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains hit by sterling strength.

text.p: LIFFE wheat futures fell on sterling's strength, traders said.
"It's purely a currency market," one trader said.
November was the most active month on wheat, with 295 lots of a total 551 traded. It last traded 1.75 stg lower at 96.25 stg.
November dominated barley trade, with 65 lots of a total 77 lots traded. It last changed hands 0.25 stg lower at 93.25 stg.
Sterling surged by around two pfennigs in afternoon trade after Britain's chancellor Gordon Brown said Britain would not be proposing to rejoin the European Exchange Rate Mechanism.
The late surge meant that all the wheat contracts, except scarcely traded front month May ended at the day's lows.

The pound rose on Brown's denial of the ERM plan because it had fallen last week on a report of possible ERM re-entry at 2.50 marks, analysts said. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
